gloss: to be rough; to be stormy; to become wild

definitions.gloss: to be rough; to be stormy
definitions.explanation: When weather, sea, or natural conditions become turbulent and violent.

definitions.gloss: to become rough; to become chapped
definitions.explanation: When skin or hands become dry and rough.

definitions.gloss: to fall into ruin; to become dilapidated
definitions.explanation: When a place becomes neglected and run-down.

definitions.gloss: to become unruly; to get wild
definitions.explanation: When a situation, meeting, or behavior becomes chaotic or rough.

examples.japanese: {台風|たいふう}で{海|うみ}が{荒|あ}れている。
examples.english: The sea is rough because of the typhoon.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}になると{手|て}が{荒|あ}れやすい。
examples.english: In winter, my hands tend to get chapped.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}が{荒|あ}れて、{収拾|しゅうしゅう}がつかなくなった。
examples.english: The meeting became chaotic and got out of control.

examples.japanese: {天気|てんき}が{荒|あ}れる{予報|よほう}だ。
examples.english: The forecast says the weather will be stormy.

examples.japanese: {波|なみ}が{荒|あ}れて{船|ふね}が{出|で}られない。
examples.english: The waves are rough, so the boats can't go out.

examples.japanese: {肌|はだ}が{荒|あ}れて{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: My skin is rough and it hurts.

examples.japanese: {唇|くちびる}が{荒|あ}れている。
examples.english: My lips are chapped.

examples.japanese: {空|あ}き{家|や}が{荒|あ}れている。
examples.english: The vacant house has fallen into disrepair.

examples.japanese: {庭|にわ}が{荒|あ}れ{放題|ほうだい}だ。
examples.english: The garden has become completely overgrown.

examples.japanese: {生活|せいかつ}が{荒|あ}れてきた。
examples.english: Their lifestyle has become chaotic.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}が{荒|あ}れた。
examples.english: The match got rough.

examples.japanese: {嵐|あらし}で{海|うみ}が{荒|あ}れ{狂|くる}う。
examples.english: The sea rages wildly in the storm.

examples.japanese: {乾燥|かんそう}で{手|て}が{荒|あ}れる。
examples.english: Dryness makes my hands rough.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}で{町|まち}が{荒|あ}れた。
examples.english: The town fell into ruin from the war.

examples.japanese: {教室|きょうしつ}が{荒|あ}れている。
examples.english: The classroom is in disorder.

examples.japanese: {風|かぜ}が{荒|あ}れて{飛行機|ひこうき}が{揺|ゆ}れた。
examples.english: The wind was rough and the plane shook.

examples.japanese: {洗剤|せんざい}で{肌|はだ}が{荒|あ}れた。
examples.english: My skin got rough from the detergent.

examples.japanese: {畑|はたけ}が{荒|あ}れて{雑草|ざっそう}だらけだ。
examples.english: The field has become overgrown with weeds.

examples.japanese: {討論|とうろん}が{荒|あ}れて{怒鳴|どな}り{合|あ}いになった。
examples.english: The debate got heated and turned into a shouting match.

examples.japanese: {廃墟|はいきょ}が{荒|あ}れ{果|は}てている。
examples.english: The ruins have completely fallen into decay.

notes:
{荒|あ}れる is an intransitive verb ({自動詞|じどうし}). The transitive pair is {荒|あ}らす (to lay waste, to devastate).

ASPECT ({ている}):
{荒|あ}れている indicates a resulting state of being rough, stormy, or dilapidated.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {海|うみ}が{荒|あ}れる - the sea becomes rough
- {天気|てんき}が{荒|あ}れる - the weather becomes stormy
- {肌|はだ}が{荒|あ}れる - skin becomes rough
- {生活|せいかつ}が{荒|あ}れる - lifestyle becomes unruly

{荒|あ}れる VS {暴|あば}れる:
{荒|あ}れる describes a state of roughness or turbulence, while {暴|あば}れる describes active violent behavior. The sea {荒|あ}れる (becomes rough), but a person {暴|あば}れる (acts violently).
